headline: New Pill Doubles Survival Time for Advanced Pancreatic Cancer
meta_description: FDA approves daraxonrasib, a twice-daily pill that doubled lifespan in pancreatic cancer patients whose tumors resisted chemotherapy, offering hope to one of m…
summary_short: A groundbreaking drug has won FDA approval after extending the lives of pancreatic cancer patients from 7 months to over 13 months, even after chemotherapy failed.
body:
Pancreatic cancer has long been one of medicine's cruelest diagnoses—fewer than 3 percent of patients survive five years past diagnosis. But a twice-daily pill called daraxonrasib is changing that grim calculus. In a phase 3 clinical trial, the drug doubled survival time in patients whose cancer had resisted chemotherapy, extending their lifespan from an average of 7 months to more than 13 months. The FDA granted approval in just 35 days, and when the results were presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology's annual meeting in Chicago in May, attending physicians and scientists rose to applaud—some with tears in their eyes.

"I have not seen anything like that before in trials we have run in pancreatic cancer," said Dr. Brian Wolpin of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston, who led the study. The drug works by targeting a protein called KRAS, which pancreatic cancer cells need to survive. For decades, scientists believed KRAS was impossible to target because of its smooth surface, but daraxonrasib found a way: it glues molecules together to create an agglomeration capable of grabbing and stopping KRAS from reaching tumors.

In rare cases, the drug has shown curative potential. One man in his 70s enrolled in the trial in 2022 watched his tumors shrink so completely that they became invisible on scans—and he remains cancer-free today. The breakthrough extends far beyond pancreatic cancer. Colon and lung cancers also depend on KRAS, and dozens of KRAS-inhibiting medications are currently being tested across the field, either alone or combined with chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Researchers are also evaluating daraxonrasib for use at earlier disease stages, signaling that this approval may represent only the beginning of a paradigm shift in cancer treatment.
quick_facts: Daraxonrasib doubled pancreatic cancer survival from 7 to 13+ months
FDA approved drug in just 35 days after phase 3 trial review
Results presented at American Society of Clinical Oncology meeting in Chicago
Drug targets KRAS protein previously thought untargetable by scientists
One patient's tumors shrank so much they became undetectable on scans
